notes.gap: S's counterexample (xc2-full-window-can-hide-a-later-span): the slot table selects kind-2 slots by start bound only, so with window [0,C) in slot 0 and [C,C+3) in slot 1 a request at p=C selected slot 0 and answered :miss although slot 1 held the octet. A false miss, never wrong bytes.
notes.fix: The per-slot plan and backing window live in the sibling stobj fn-xcw (plans array; windows array of fn-xcw-win, congruent to fn-ew-buffer), and fn-xc-span-at walks the candidates itself in one call: lookup from FROM, try the selected slot's own row, on a decline continue from slot+1, measure = slot count - from. fn-xc-install-window-bytes stores the plan and the staged window with the slot; fn-xc-init-windows refuses more windows than rows by name (:refused-window-rows).
notes.signature: (fn-xc-span-at from ledger file eoff elen poff plen trailer p end fn-xcs fn-xcc fn-xcw fn-ew-span) -> (mv word count slot fn-ew-span fn-xcs fn-xcc), word :span or :miss; (fn-xc-install-window-bytes token plan fn-xcs fn-xcc fn-xcw fn-ew-buffer) -> (mv word slot evicted fn-xcs fn-xcc fn-xcw); (fn-xc-init-windows ne nw fn-xcs fn-xcc) -> (mv word fn-xcs fn-xcc).
notes.old_export_deleted: The earlier fn-xc-span-at (plan and window arguments) is deleted, not twinned. Its K1 statements follow from the new ones by instantiation: fn-xc-span-at-is-the-returned-bytes (C2) is the old statement with plan and window read from the answering slot's row; fn-xc-span-at-answers-an-owed-hit is restated over the walk and follows from the covered-slot keystone (fn-xc-span-at-answers-a-covered-slot, C1) with the answered slot equal to the first candidate (fn-xc-span-at-answers-no-earlier-than-the-first-candidate); fn-xc-span-at-hit-touches-only-the-selected-slot now holds without its span hypothesis (a miss names no slot and touches none).
notes.stale_row: fn-pwc-span-at checks the row's plan against the slot's token (fn-pwr-plan-matches-token) before copying; fn-xc-span-at-answers-from-a-matching-slot exports that check, xcst-stale-row-answers-miss shows a row written for another token answers :miss, and the unchecked statement is must-fail.
